recipes.name: Eclair Cake with Chocolate Ganache
ingredients_raw: 2 (3.5 ounce) packages instant vanilla pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Chill a mixing bowl in the freezer.

Combine water, butter, and salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium; stir in flour. Cook and stir until mixture pulls away from the sides of the pan and forms a ball. Transfer to a mixing bowl and beat in eggs, one at a time, until fully incorporated. Spread dough evenly into the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes. (The dough will rise and make a boat shape, but should drop as it cools.) Cool completely on a wire rack.

Pour 2 cups cold cream into the chilled bowl; whip until cream thickens, about 1 minute. Stir in confectioners’ sugar and vanilla. Continue whipping until stiff peaks form. Chill whipped cream in the refrigerator until ready to use.
Combine milk and pudding mix in a separate bowl; stir until creamy. Fold in whipped cream. Spread filling over cooled crust and refrigerate.

Place chocolate in a heat-proof bowl. Bring 1 cup cream in a small saucepan over medium heat almost to a boil; pour over chocolate and let sit for 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Cool until thickened, about 10 minutes.
Pour chocolate ganache over cream filling, spreading to cover the entire surface. Refrigerate cake before serving at least 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Eclair Cake with Chocolate Ganache
raw_recipe.description: This eclair cake with chocolate ganache recipe features a delicious, creamy filling on top of a light choux pastry glazed with a rich chocolate ganache.

review.reviewBody: This cake is amazing. It's one of the first desserts I've made that was completely finished by my family. It is even better the next day, so I would recommend making it the day before you plan on serving it so that the flavors really meld. The ganache should be properly chilled in order to get the eclair texture. I used semi-sweet chocolate chips and the ganache tasted great. Please don't substitute anything else for this crust, either--the crust what makes the cake taste like a true eclair. The pastry shell stays firm enough to support the filling without getting soft or soggy. I have tried other eclair cake recipes that call for graham cracker crumbs in layers and they do not have the delicious and realistic eclair taste that this recipe has. Freeze the beater(s) along with the mixing bowl and your whipped cream will form stiff peaks faster. And make sure your bowl is completely clean before attempting to whip the cream; that's why you whip it before you mix the pudding. Fold in pudding with a spatula and don't overmix and it will stay fluffy. Hope this helps!

This was very, very good! Our new favorite dessert, indeed. I'd never made choux pastry before and was intrigued to try a new style of pastry. Very easy to do, especially if you're familiar with the method for roux (cooking flour with butter for sauces and such). Baked the pastry for about 8 minutes longer than directed and it was perfect; let it bake until even the bottom is golden brown, the sides will most certainly puff up and create the desired boat effect. Did not add the confectioner's sugar or vanilla to the whipped cream as I knew it would be too rich for our taste buds but this was the only "change" made to the original recipe. Be sure to fold the whipped cream into the pudding, don't just scramble-mix it together. The ganache was perfect, especially after chilling on top of the cake overnight. This dessert is perfect for company or just all to yourself! We did not feel it tasted faux or plastic in any way. UPDATE: Made this again with vanilla and banana cream pudding together and also sprinkled sweet roasted walnuts over top of the ganache. This brought it to an entirely new level of scrumptiousness!

This recipe was as good as I'd hoped for! I wish I could give this one more than 5 stars, it truly deserves it! I was a bit skeptical because of the instant pudding, I try to stay away from ingredients like that to ensure a true homemade/scratch flavor. No fake flavors in this recipe! This was my 1st time making choux pastry, and I'm pleased to report that it was so easy. I really don't know why reviewers claimed that this recipe required many steps, many bowls/pans, utensils, etc. I didn't feel that it was any more than most desserts require. It was also a quick and simple recipe overall, IMHO. My only change to the recipe was to use semi-sweet chocolate instead of bittersweet due to what I had on hand. I had no problems with "runny" chocolate, as other reviewers described. Please note: the filling uses "heavy whipping cream" while the ganache uses "heavy cream"...they are not the same. I only had heavy whipping cream and no heavy cream on hand, so I used a substitute: 3/4 c. milk and 1/4 c. butter=1 c. heavy cream. Because there are only 2 of us eating this dessert, I made 1/2 of the recipe and used an 8" x 8" pan. It made a beautiful, thick presentation that I will be proud to serve at future dinners. If you follow the instructions of this recipe, you will be rewarded with an awesome eclair cake that is truly delectable! My husband loved it, so I'll be prompted to make it again and again! ;-)

Delicious! I substituted the 2 packages of vanilla pudding with one portion of the 'pastry cream' recipe on allrecipes by Kevin Ryan. I also sprinkled medium roast coffee grounds before I poured the chocolate sauce on top. It is the best cake ever and holds its shape even when cutting and serving. It was a huge hit! Thank you. (Requires 5 stars with these little changes)

I'm giving this 5 stars for taste and presentation, although I will make slight modifications next time.
If you mound the dough more towards the centre, you'll get a better baked shape. Next time I'll use half the filling ingredients. I don't prefer a Ganache for chocolate eclairs. I made one from Good Housekeeping that is better (in our opinion)(2tbsp butter or margarine, 2squares unsweetened Chocolate, 2tbsp hot water, 1-1.5 c. icing sugar).
To make it like a real chocolate eclair, slice the baked pastry in half horizontally, pour in the filling, cover with the top layer and ice the top layer. I served 14 people with this cake. Everybody raved about it.

To cut down on the number of bowls, I left the water/butter/flour mixture in the saucepan and then used my portable mixer to beat in the eggs. I baked the batter in a round cake pan and then split it in half once it had cooled. For those who think this recipe is too "eggy", this will allow you to scoop out some of the inards and then let the shell dry out a bit before adding the fillings. As others have suggested, I used French Vanilla pudding mix. I couldn't find bittersweet chocolate at the grocers, so used semi-sweet. Fresh strawberries and raspberries are in season so that made a nice garnish along with some mint leaves. Yum.

This was a hit for our Mother's Day family party! I made the filling with the Pastry Cream recipe on here, once it was soft set I folded the whipped cream into it as you would with the pudding mix. I have already given a copy of the recipes to other family members and it is on the list of favorites for everyone!
Tastes just like a chocolate eclair. I cut the recipe in half and made it in a 9" pie plate. Very good and easy to make.

This is my son's favourite dessert, it truly tastes like a huge eclair, it looks really fancy but easy to make, definitely make the day before to let it set properly for easier serving. The only issue is the ganache, the proportions as written result in a soupy consistency that does not set, 1 cup chocolate chips is 6 oz by weight which is too little with 8 fluid oz whipping cream, I use 8 oz bittersweet chocolate chopped by weight to 4 fluid oz whipping cream and it turns out perfect.

This has become a family favorite. I make it according to the recipe. I use half and half for the heavy cream in the ganache. For the vanilla pudding meixture, I use 2% milk. And of course, heavy whipping cream for the whipped cream that is folded into the pudding mixture. I also use Ghiradelli bittersweet baking chocolate. Turns out great!

The filling recipe was extremely mealy and inedible. I've made whipped cream many times with normal sugar, which always comes out smooth and creamy. But THIS time with the confectioners sugar, it came out tasting all starchy and even grainy. And the pudding didn't help either, like it was a pathetic attempt to mask the bad whipped cream. The filling neither tasted like proper whipped cream or pudding, just tasted like disappointment and a failure to produce either one. Grainy, starchy, overly sweet. I could've just made a normal batch of whipped cream and it would've come out great, you know, tasting like an ACTUAL eclair. What a waste of expensive cream. Next time I'll trust my instincts. On a more positive note, the eclair pastry shell was good. But that's about it.
I'm going to make this with graham cracker crust (sort of like a cheesecake). Can I use cool whip instead of heavy cream?

My 16yo daughter made this with one substitution. She used Bob’s gf all purpose flour for the crust in order to make it gluten free. Other than that, no changes. It is absolutely delicious. Turned out perfect! 😍

I loved that this cake is made with a true choux pastry crust! It's so easy and just really makes it more 'authentically eclair'! The only thing I would change is the filling. I felt there was too much whipped cream--it sort of diluted the flavor of the filling, and made it too soft (mine never really set up properly). I think I would at least half the whipped cream amount. I might also play around with using a real pastry cream filling; or maybe like another reviewer did, and try a cheesecake filling. Other than that, this was super easy to make; and had major wow factor. Will make again with a few changes. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

This recipe didn’t thrill me. Had 2 pieces with the 2nd being the next day because several reviewers said they thought it was better the second day. Big disappointment. Bland flavor, chewy cake, not enough chocolate taste, way too much cream/pudding filling. Sorry, just not worth the calories for us.
Raves from everyone! Spectacular celebratory dessert.

Followed the recipe exactly as written and it turned out fantastic! My husband, who never eats a lot of desserts had three pieces and told me it was the best dessert I’ve ever made. Thank you for sharing!
After the first time I served this I have always been asked to make it again. It's SOOO easy, and SOOO good! I won't change a thing!
